outcome: Receipt of maternal interventions (cesarean delivery, maternal hospital transfer, antenatal corticosteroid administration)
Receipt of neonatal interventions (neonatal intensive care unit admission, surfactant administration, antibiotic administration, assisted ventilation)
cohort: Live births in the United States at 22(0/6) to 23(6/7) weeks of gestation from 2012 to 2016
finding: Non-Hispanic Black race was associated with not receiving maternal interventions, while private insurance, singleton pregnancy, and small for gestational age were associated with not receiving neonatal interventions at 22 and 23 weeks of gestation, highlighting the influence of sociodemographic and pregnancy factors on periviable birth management decisions.
mod_finding: Non-Hispanic Black race was associated with receiving no maternal interventions, including cesarean delivery.
